April 2009 # Wave of optimism upon a sea of despair - Copper prices broke through the $4,000/t barrier in March, as the market reacted to record Chinese imports and falling LME stocks. Chinese imports have been boosted by a tight scrap market and stockbuilding by the State Reserve Bureau (SRB). - Demand, though, remains terrible. CRU is now forecasting a decline in world refined copper demand of more than 10% for 2009 as a whole. Only China offers prospects for any significant growth, with some initial signs that it should avoid the meltdown being experienced elsewhere. - High prices and falling costs mean that further production cutbacks have been avoided, but stocks (whether reported or not) are rising rapidly. Chinese buying, particularly by the SRB, should moderate with prices at $4,000/t. When it does, dismal global demand will cause the wave of optimism to break and push prices back towards $3,000/t. |The supply/demand

wn in LME stocks and to strengthening Chinese imports of refined copper. China’s imports were boosted by major purchases by the State Reserves Bureau (SRB) and by tight scrap availability. The weakening of the US dollar versus other currencies, as a result of quantitative easing and concerns over inflation, helped the price through the $4,000/t barrier on 19th March for the first time since midNovember. However, there is little evidence of tightness, as the market has remained in contango throughout the run up in prices since the low in December 2008. Copper prices have risen by almost 30% since the beginning of the year, more than any other LME metal. As financial investors continue to look for growth opportunities in difficult market conditions, there has been a renewed wave of speculative interest in copper as an investment product. However, it may not be too long before this wave breaks. It is abundantly clear that fundamental consumption remains extremely weak. CRU now forecasts that 2009 refined copper demand will see the worst annual contraction since at least 1975, and possibly the worst since 1945. Although SRB purchases have supported the price rise recently, these are likely to cease until the copper price returns to a lower level. Despite the fall in the copper price over the past few days, copper continues to look expensive given the dire global economic and demand situation. ## **State Reserve Bureau purchases are likely to pause until price falls** As reported in our last monitor, a significant factor supporting the price has been purchasing by China’s SRB. The SRB is extremely secretive about its purchasing, but there is a general view that it will be taking delivery of at least 300,000t of refined copper in the first half of 2009. We believe that this metal may have been booked at the end of last year, when prices were just over $3,000/t. So far in 2009 SRB purchases have accounted for a significant portion of Chinese imports of refined copper. Furthermore, there is speculation that the SRB could be in the market for another 300,000-900,000t over the next couple of years. The timing of additional purchases will be subject to price developments and we believe they are unlikely to return to the market until the price falls back towards $3,000/t. Therefore, future SRB purchases may help support prices at around $3,000/t rather than at current levels. Tight

scrap availability and domestic production problems in late 2008 and early 2009 have also caused China to import more cathode.  In the first two months of 2009, Chinese imports of copper scrap plummeted 53% year-on-year.  CRU estimates that reduced scrap availability will bolster world refined copper consumption by at least 500,000t in 2009, of which the majority will come in China.  The scrap market is tight due to lower industrial output leading to lower generation of process scrap, and there is less end use scrap as fewer products are discarded.  With a much lower copper price, the incentive to collect and process scrap is also reduced.  Traders are also hoarding scrap in the hope that prices will rise in the future.  In the case of China, there has been additional reluctance to ship to the country following defaults in Q4 2008, with

US scrap exporters now demanding a significant deposit (70%) for copper scrap in many cases.  However, despite scrap tightness, as smelter production revives, continued refined imports at current levels could push the market into short term oversupply from the end of March. 

## **CRU forecasts double-digit fall in world refined demand in 2009** 

CRU’s latest market forecast calls for refined copper demand to fall by more than 10% in 2009 (the exact numbers are currently being finalised).  The last time world demand registered a double-digit fall was in 1975, when it fell 11.2%.  This year’s decline could well be worse still, making it the largest fall since 1945, when demand fell by 14.7%.  In the Great Depression, global copper consumption saw three years of double-digit declines in the period 1930-32. 

We are nearly through Q1 and entering what is normally the peak season for copper demand.  However, outside China, key indicators of industrial activity and commodities demand suggest that fundamental conditions are very weak.  Freight rates remain well down on last year, and most commodity prices have plummeted, with other industrial products such as steel performing much worse than copper.  Sentiment remains extremely poor.  Moody’s global survey reports that business confidence is at -29 points as of 20<sup>th</sup> March, with pessimism extending across all industries, particularly manufacturing. 

The only firm copper products data available for 2009 shows declines of more than 20% for Japanese wire and cable shipments in January.  Plant closures, consolidation and restructuring continue as firms respond to the downturn.  So far in March, in the US alone, such announcements have included: Rea Magnet Wire to cease production at one of its Indiana plants, Belden to close its interconnect plant in Virginia, Coleman Cable to close a wire and cable plant in Massachusetts, interconnects manufacturer Tyco to undertake major job cuts, and International Wire to idle two plants in New Hampshire. 

##

**Demand hopes rest on China** 

China is one of only a handful of countries where we anticipate narrowly positive consumption growth in 2009.  However, we believe demand is contracting year-on-year in the first quarter.  Therefore China’s ability to achieve growth this year will depend on the effectiveness of economic stimulus measures, particularly infrastructure spending and increased bank lending, to boost the power, automotive, railway and construction sectors which will need to offset weaker demand from export markets. 

Given the implementation periods required for these measures, we are unlikely to see a major impact on demand until at least Q3 2009.  However, state infrastructure bodies may make some copper purchases in advance of actual requirements.  The latest official data gives some cautious signs for optimism.  Power cable production rose by 17% y-o-y in the first two months of 2009 to 2.4M km.  However, this is likely to be largely due to delivery of orders placed last year and some base effects have to be included from comparisons to a very weak start to 2008.  Official growth statistics should be treated with caution, but were generally positive in February.  Metal products output was up 12.1% y-o-y after contraction in January, and manufacture of machinery and transport equipment both registered double-digit growth in the month. Output of communications, computer and other electronic equipment was up 0.3% in February after a sharp fall in January. 

New Chinese fabricating projects in wirerod and flat rolled products also lend optimism to the view that refined demand will continue to rise in the country.  Copper tube manufacturers currently face weak demand from the air conditioner sector.  However, it is anticipated that new air conditioner efficiency regulations will be launched shortly, which should lead to greater copper usage per unit. 

One area where government initiatives, including bank lending, already seem to be having a positive impact is in the automotive sector.  In February, Chinese vehicle sales were 827,600, up 24.7% y-o-y and up 12.4% m-o-m.  Vehicle output was also up 23.1% y-o-y to 807,000 units according to the China Association of

Automobile Manufacturers.  Policies introduced earlier in 2009 included the scrapping of some road fees and halving of sales taxes on small vehicles.  Most recently, China announced measures to consolidate car manufacturing into a few companies and to boost demand by encouraging the development of environmentally friendly cars, as part of its efforts to keep sales growing at an annual rate of 10% over the next three years.  Although there will be some benefit to Chinese automotive component manufacturers from the domestic market, they will still be badly hit by the collapse in vehicle production in most export markets. 

## **European premia up on China buying**

Premia in Europe widened to $20-50/t on the back of increased buying from China. European LME stocks fell by 12% since end-February through 25th March, as stocks flowed to China as a result of the positive LME-SHFE arbitrage. Traders have also reported some selling to the Middle East. Aside from Asian related activity, there was very little physical trade reported in Europe. In the US, premiums remained extremely low at around ¢35/lb, although there were reports of slightly more interest than earlier in the year. Despite stock declines elsewhere in the world, as of 25th March US (COMEX and LME) stocks were up 14% since the beginning of the month. China refined imports

There was only one new Chilean tender over the past month. Codelco awarded 6,000t of CCC and other LME registered cathode for delivery over the April to June period, achieving a premium of $100/t. The quotation period was the month following contractual month of shipment and payment terms were 30 days after the bill of lading date. ## **Lower costs and hedging continue to support supply, for now** Copper’s price recovery so far in 2009 has held off the need for further cutbacks in mine supply. The only recent new cutback announcements have been at high-cost mines in Zambia (see industry news). Lower mining costs have also helped cushion the blow of lower prices for copper producers. Using CRU’s valuebased costing method, our newly released **2009 Copper Mine Cost Report** foresees a 27% reduction in average business costs this year as the costs of consumables, fuel, power, royalties and freight fall. This compares to an increase in costs of 11% in 2008. In addition, a number of higher-cost mines have put in place hedging arrangements which have helped them absorb the cost of price falls. For instance, KGHM has hedged a quarter of H1 output at $6,000/t and Teck Cominco has hedged 55% of its copper production through March at about $5,300/t. These hedges have enabled them to maintain profitable production even though the copper price may have fallen below their cost of production. Some of these companies will likely come under renewed pressure to cut back production when these hedges expire. Going forward, higher-cost mines continue to attempt to put in place hedges to try and maintain margins should prices fall further. For example, First Quantum has a six-month rolling hedge on up to 55% of its copper output. Therefore, hedges are likely to cause a time lag between any future fall in price and further cuts in production. Data released by the **Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers’ Association** showed that shipments of copper wire and cable in January plummeted to 53,100t, down by 21.2% y-o-y. The biggest decrease was in the automotive industry, which fell by 39.3% y-o-y to 4,500t. Electric wire and cable deliveries in 2008 amounted to 815,835t of copper, down by 5% y-o-y. The decline in Q4 2008 was 14% y-o-y. According to the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** , rolled copper products shipments plunged by 5.6% y-o-y in 2008 to 946,986t, with a dramatic contraction in Q4. That was attributed not only to the ailing auto industry but also to the recently hit cell phone and computer markets. ## **Some promising investment prospects in China for copper semis** **China** is planning to spend RMB403.3B in 2009 and RMB426.7B in 2010 for power grid projects. However, the positive effects on refined demand are expected to develop gradually. **Fujian Nanping Sun Cable Co., Ltd.** will build a 100kt/y copper wirerod project in **Shanghang** . According to company plans, the first stage will be complete by September with output capacity of 30kt/y of 8mm copper wirerod and other wire products. Upon completion of the second stage production capacity will amount to 100kt/y. Market participants are bullish on the RMB4 trillion economic stimulus package to boost domestic consumption. **Chinalco Luoyang Copper Co., Ltd.** is work

ing on a 100kt/y high-precision copper plate, sheet and strip (PSS) project. According to **Antaike** , the project is expected to start operations at the end of 2009. When completed, the company will have doubled its copper PSS output capacity to 200kt/y. ## **More plant closures, production cuts, layoffs and short-time working** The copper semis market has been hit by the downturn in the automotive, electronics, construction, air conditioning and industrial applications sectors. As a result, manufacturers are adjusting capacity. **Wieland-Werke** will introduce short-time working for 3,450 staff. Earlier plans considered short-time working for 1,100 out of its 4,300 employees in **Germany** . **Sumitomo Light Metal Industries Ltd.** is expecting to cut its domestic copper tube output by 30% in Q1 2009 compared to the same period in 2008 and its original plans. The company is shutting down operations for two days a month in **Toyokawa City, Aichi** . **Belden Inc.** will close its plant in **Midlothian, Virginia** , by July 2009. ures|| # Technical Analysis In the very short term, copper has a decision to make. In order to continue the uptrend that has been evidence since December, the 3-month price must respect the support at $3,930/t, which has held twice. If it fails to hold here, the next support levels are at $3,860/t and then $3,720/t. If support holds, the market should move back above the recent high at $4,080/t then challenge $4,131/t. Although the major technical indicators are broadly neutral, the stochastics are close to crossing. If the market remains steady, this crossing will generate a cautious buy signal. The picture on the short term chart is neutral with a slight bias towards the upside. Longer term, the market has moved above key resistance at $3,700/t and is now in a broad zone leading up to resistance at $5,250/t. The possible behaviour of copper in this zone can be anticipated by analysing its performance on the way up – in the second half of 2005 copper picked up momentu

m, with volatility and monthly trading ranges increasing throughout.  The resistance at $5,250/t was the mid-point at which the market found interim support, after the first failure during the topping formation, and has a great deal of significance. 

Overall, while the market may look lacklustre and inconclusive in the short term, there are some very clear trigger points close to current price levels.  The support zone around $3,700/t is a key point and if it holds there is a possibility (from a technical viewpoint) that some relatively unimpeded progress may be achieved.

# Industry News 

## **Production** 















- **Mopani Copper Mines (MCM)** plans to put its **Mufulira** and **Nkana** mines on a care and maintenance basis in April 2009 due to a lack of profitability as a result of falling copper prices.  In response, the Zambian government has asked MCM to voluntarily surrender its assets to the government to maintain operations and preserve jobs.  The company has stated that it only plans to restart production when the copper price reaches around US$5,500/t.  MCM will continue to operate its Mufulira smelter. In 2008, the Mufulira mine produced 60,000t of contained copper and the Nkana mine produced 80,000t. 

- In February, **OZ Minerals** delivered its first copper-gold concentrate from **Prominent Hill** following commissioning as scheduled.  Prominent Hill is expected to produce some 85,000t of copper in concentrate this year. 

- **Anvil Mining** has stated in its Q4 2008 results that copper production for 2008 declined by 13% year-on-year, to 41,354t. Copper sales decreased over the same period by 27% to US$191.2M. The company put its Dikulushi mine on care and maintenance in December, but plans to continue with construction and commissioning of the Kinsevere Stage II SXEW project. 

- Full year copper production for **Zijin Mining** increased by 30% year-on-year in 2008 to 61,400t, of which around 10,000t were copper cathodes and the rest copper in concentrate.  The company, which owns four Chinese copper mines, also announced plans to increase copper metal production by 36% to 83,500t in 2009. 

- Zambia’s **Luanshya Copper Mines** ( **LCM** ) is currently the subject of acquisition bids from a number of interested parties, and **Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines-Investment Holdings (ZCCM-IH)** is reported to be in discussion with LCM management about increasing its 15% stake in LCM. There are hopes that a takeover will lead to a restart in production at the **Baluba** mine and **Chambishi Metals Plc,** which were shut down in December. 

- The lower house of Chile’s parliament approved a bill on 17 March to modernise and invest in the state copper mining company **Codelco** . The bill calls for the appointment of four independent members of the board of directors, four chosen by the country’s President, an

d one to be chosen by the company’s workers, and for a capitalisation programme of up to US$1B to stimulate growth and employment. It will also set minimum qualifications for board members. The bill will next be voted on by the Senate. 

- On 7<sup>th</sup> March 2009, **Sterlite Industries** (a subsidiary of the London-listed **Vedanta Resources)** announced that it had signed a new agreement with **Asarco.** Sterlite Industries will buy all of the operating assets of Asarco with a cash payment of US$1.1B and a senior secured non-interest bearing promissory note for US$600M payable over nine years, which includes US$20M/y for seven years and a terminal payment of US$460M at the end of the ninth year.  The assets to be acquired consist of three open-pit copper mines and their mills and SXEW, a copper smelter in Arizona, a copper refinery, rod and cake plants and a precious metals plant in Texas.  Sterlite Industries previously slashed its bid from last year's offer of US$2.6B to US$1.4-1.5B a week before the announcement. However, Sterlite Industries’ rival, **Grupo Mexico** , which bought Asarco for US$2.2B in 1999 before Asarco filed for bankruptcy due to several lawsuits on environmental issues in 2005, said that it was still interested in recovering Asarco, after fighting in court over the case for months.

## **Exploration and Development** 











- **Vale** has announced the completion of a deal with **African Rainbow Mining Ltd** ( **ARM** ) to operate and develop the assets of **TEAL Exploration and Mining Inc** ( **TEAL** ) on a 50:50 joint venture basis. The assets consist of copper and cobalt exploration and development programmes in the African copperbelt in Zambia and DR Congo. 

- The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) announced on 25 March that it will not obstruct the proposed transaction between **Rio Tinto** and **Aluminium Corporation of China (Chinalco** ), and rejected arguments from some who fear that the company would act to lower iron ore price **s,** which would be to the advantage of Chinese steel mills. Earlier in the month, the Australian government announced an extension of their review into the transaction, and this will now continue through to late June. If the transaction is agreed, it will include a US$19.5B in total investment in Rio Tinto, involving an increased shareholding by Chinalco in both Rio Tinto and some strategic assets, and a strategic partnership between both companies. 

- In March, it was reported that the Mongolian government is scheduled to consider giving approval for **Ivanhoe Mines Ltd** and other companies to begin mining at the **Oyu Tolgoi** copper and gold mine in March. **Rio Tinto** owns a minority stake in Ivanhoe Mines Ltd with an option to increase it to US$2.3B for a 46.65% stake. The parties were expected to sign an investment agreement in March

for Ivanhoe to benefit from demand in China, but the decision has been delayed and is not now expected before April. The Oyu Tolgoi deposit is one of the largest copper ore resources in the world and CRU expects it to produce some 360,000t/y of copper in concentrates. 

- In March, it was reported that **Chinalco Peru** (subsidiary of Chinese Chinalco) started the construction of the **Kingsmill** tunnel plant to treat acid water from the Morococha district.  This plant is part of the social and environmental commitments of its **Toromocho** project.  In mid-November, Chinalco announced it has obtained a US$2.2B loan for the development of it Toromocho project in Peru.  The capital cost estimate recently increased to US$2.15B from US$1.5B.  The Toromocho project is forecast to produce 260,000t/y of copper in concentrate starting up in 2012. 

- After imposing a ban on all mining and exploration activities in Ecuador last April, the Ecuadorian government has advised **Corriente Resources Inc.** that it may resume operations. The Canadian company has four copper and copper-gold porphyry deposits in the country, which are being developed under the titles of the **Mirador** project and the **Panantza-San Carlos** project.
